windows_11.applies_to: New Windows 11 laptops/desktops on first boot (out-of-box experience, OOBE), mainly Home and Pro for personal use. Exact screens vary by Windows 11 version, edition, manufacturer, and whether the device is managed by a work or school organisation.

steps.detail: On the first setup screens, pick your country or region, language, and keyboard layout when prompted. Setup may offer a second keyboard layout; add one only if you use it, otherwise skip that prompt.
steps.title: Choose region and keyboard

steps.detail: Choose your Wi-Fi network and enter its password, or plug in Ethernet if the laptop has it or you have an adapter. An internet connection is part of documented first setup for consumer editions (see honest_notes), and it is also needed for updates and some features.
steps.title: Connect to a network

steps.detail: Sign in with an existing Microsoft account, or create one during setup if prompted. Signing in is what Microsoft documents as bringing your files, settings and Microsoft services with you to the new device. Complete any extra verification the account asks for.
steps.title: Sign in with a Microsoft account

steps.detail: Some Windows 11 versions and manufacturers show a screen to name the device during setup. If you see it, use a short, recognisable name. If you do not see it, do not worry — the name can be changed later in Settings. See honest_notes: Microsoft's consumer support pages consulted for this guide do not settle this step.
steps.title: Name the PC, if setup offers it

steps.detail: Setup presents privacy choices for the device (historically including things such as location, diagnostic data, inking and typing improvement, and tailored experiences). Read each screen instead of tapping through, and choose the more private option if you do not want that data use. You can change these choices later in Settings.
steps.title: Make the privacy choices shown during setup

steps.detail: Follow any remaining prompts (for example PIN / Windows Hello if offered for your model, and any manufacturer or Microsoft service offers). Decline offers you do not want. Setup finishes at the Windows desktop.
steps.title: Finish setup and reach the desktop

steps.detail: Open Start > Settings > Windows Update and select Check for updates. Install what is offered, restart when asked, then go back and check again. Repeat until Windows Update reports no further updates are offered. Keep the laptop plugged in and online while this runs.
steps.title: Run Windows Update until current

steps.detail: Worth reviewing after setup: Start > Settings > Privacy & security. Check Location (which apps may use your location), Diagnostics & feedback (turn off optional diagnostic data and tailored experiences if you do not want them), and the advertising ID / personalisation page — labelled General on some builds and Recommendations & offers on newer builds — where you can turn off letting apps show personalised ads using your advertising ID. Also review app permissions for Camera, Microphone, Contacts and Calendar, and turn off individual apps you do not want to have access. Note: Microsoft says these permission lists mainly cover Microsoft Store apps; desktop apps may not appear in them and control access in their own settings.
steps.title: Review privacy settings in Settings

steps.detail: Microsoft Support documents creating a USB recovery drive after setup: search the taskbar for 'Create a recovery drive', open the tool, keep 'Back up system files to the recovery drive' selected, choose a USB drive and select Create. Creating it erases that USB drive, so use a blank one or move its files first.
steps.title: Optional: make a recovery drive

honest_notes: Local account — stated honestly: Microsoft's current Windows 11 specifications say Windows 11 Home, and Windows 11 Pro for personal use, require internet connectivity and a Microsoft account during initial device setup. Microsoft does not document a consumer local-account path in Home OOBE in the pages consulted for this guide.

Required diagnostic data cannot be turned completely off in consumer Settings in the way optional diagnostic data can; the documented review action is to turn optional data / tailored experiences off if you do not want them.
disclaimers: Workarounds for a local account exist online, but they are not Microsoft's documented consumer flow, so this guide does not give a hack tutorial for them.

Pro for work or school is different from Pro for personal use: organisation setup can involve joining a work or school account / domain instead of a personal Microsoft account, but the consumer Microsoft Support pages consulted here do not document that OOBE path step by step, so the exact screens are unsettled in this guide and will depend on the organisation.
PC naming during OOBE is unsettled in the official pages consulted: it appears on some versions/builds and not others, so it is presented as 'if offered' rather than as a guaranteed step.

Privacy page labels vary by Windows 11 build: the advertising ID and related personalisation controls have appeared under Privacy & security > General and, on newer builds, under Recommendations & offers / personalised offers pages. Use the labels shown on the device.

macos.applies_to: New Mac laptops (MacBook Air / MacBook Pro) on first startup with Setup Assistant. Exact screens, and whether Touch ID, Apple Pay and FileVault are offered during setup, vary by model, chip and macOS version.

steps.detail: Turn the Mac on. Setup Assistant starts the first time. Choose your country or region — Apple uses this to set language and time zone. Accessibility options are available early in setup if you need them (for example VoiceOver guidance).
steps.title: Start Setup Assistant and choose country or region

steps.detail: Choose your Wi-Fi network and enter its password if asked. If you are using wired Ethernet, choose Other Network Options instead. You can change the network later from the Wi-Fi menu / System Settings.
steps.title: Connect to Wi-Fi

steps.detail: Setup Assistant offers Migration Assistant during setup. If this is a first Mac or you want a clean start, choose the option not to transfer information now. If you are moving from another Mac, a PC, a Time Machine backup or another disk, choose that source and follow the prompts. If you skip it, you can still transfer later with Migration Assistant in Applications > Utilities.
steps.title: Decide whether to transfer information

steps.detail: Sign in with your Apple Account (the account formerly called Apple ID) if prompted, and complete any verification. Apple notes some setup items can be skipped and done later — its guide gives Apple Pay and Screen Time as examples where choosing 'Set up later' can make sense during first setup.
steps.title: Sign in with your Apple Account

steps.detail: Read and agree to the macOS Terms and Conditions when shown. Create the local computer (administrator) account for the Mac — full name, account name and a strong password you will remember. This password is also important for FileVault (see below).
steps.title: Agree to Terms and Conditions and create your computer account

steps.detail: Work through the choice screens Setup Assistant shows on your model/version, which can include Location Services / time zone, sharing analytics / crash and usage data with Apple and developers, Screen Time, Siri, and appearance. Choose 'Set up later' / decline sharing where that is what you want; these choices can be changed later in System Settings.
steps.title: Make Siri, analytics and other choice screens

steps.detail: On models with Touch ID, Setup Assistant can offer fingerprint setup during first setup, and Apple Pay setup if you add a supported card. Both vary by model, and Apple Pay needs a verified card, so it is reasonable to choose 'Set up later' and finish these in System Settings after setup if you prefer.
steps.title: Set up Touch ID and Apple Pay, if your model offers them

steps.detail: FileVault may be offered during setup. Apple documents it as an extra security layer: on Macs with Apple silicon or a T2 chip the data is already encrypted automatically, and turning FileVault on means someone cannot decrypt or access the data without the login password. If you turn it on, choose how to unlock the disk if you forget your password — allow your iCloud / Apple Account to unlock it, or create a recovery key. If you choose a recovery key, copy it exactly and keep it somewhere safe away from the Mac and not only on the encrypted disk. If FileVault was not offered in Setup Assistant, check it in Apple menu > System Settings > Privacy & Security > FileVault.
steps.title: Turn on FileVault if offered, or check it right after setup

steps.detail: Open Apple menu > System Settings > General > Software Update. Software Update checks automatically and only offers updates compatible with your Mac. If updates are shown, click Update Now (or Upgrade Now for a newer major macOS version), enter the administrator password if asked, and let the Mac restart if needed. In the same place you can review Automatic Updates options, including downloading updates and installing macOS and security updates automatically.
steps.title: Update macOS after setup

disclaimers: Apple does not publish one single support page that lists every current Setup Assistant screen in order for all Mac laptops; this flow combines Apple's model Setup Assistant guides with Apple's separate Software Update and FileVault support pages, so screen order can differ slightly by macOS version.
Touch ID, Apple Pay, Siri / Apple Intelligence, Screen Time and FileVault prompts vary by model, chip, region and macOS version — this guide marks them as 'if offered' instead of guaranteeing them.

Migration Assistant sources and wording vary by version (another Mac, PC, Time Machine backup or startup disk); the settled point from Apple is that transferring is optional during setup and can also be done later.

Whether FileVault is presented as a setup screen or is already on / needs turning on in System Settings was not settled for every model by the Apple pages consulted; the safe documented action is to check Privacy & Security > FileVault after setup.

chromeos.applies_to: New Chromebooks (and Chromeboxes, with a monitor, keyboard and mouse) on first setup. Exact wording, Google Play availability and Linux support vary by model, ChromeOS version, and whether the device is managed by a work or school.

steps.detail: If the battery is separate, install it first, then press the power button. Have your Google Account username and password and internet access ready — Google lists those as what you need for setup.
steps.title: Turn on the Chromebook

steps.detail: Follow the on-screen instructions: select the language shown to set language and keyboard settings, turn on Accessibility features if you need them, choose your network (Wi-Fi) and connect, then accept the terms of service.
steps.title: Choose language, keyboard, network and accept terms

steps.detail: Enter your Google Account email or phone number and password. The first account to sign in becomes the Chromebook owner. If you use 2-Step Verification, enter the code sent to your chosen device when prompted. Once you sign in, your bookmarks, extensions and apps appear automatically.
steps.title: Sign in with a Google Account

steps.detail: If you do not have a Google Account, create one — on some Chromebooks you can select More options > Create new account during setup. To use the Chromebook without an account, select Browse as Guest. Guest browsing is not the same as setting the Chromebook up as owner.
steps.title: If you have no account, or want to browse without one

steps.detail: ChromeOS automatically checks for and downloads operating system updates when connected to the internet. To finish a downloaded update, use the 'Update available' / 'Update device' notification at the bottom right and select Restart. To check yourself: turn the Chromebook on, connect to Wi-Fi, select the time at the bottom right > Settings, select About ChromeOS at the bottom left, and under Google ChromeOS select Check for updates — if an update is found it downloads automatically, then restart to finish. Keep it plugged in to avoid interruption, and note that on mobile data you may get an alert about data use.
steps.title: Let ChromeOS updates work, and check manually

steps.detail: After setup, open the time at the bottom right > Settings > Apps > Google Play Store and select Turn on if that option is shown, then follow the prompts and accept the Play terms. Menu labels vary by ChromeOS version. Not every model supports Android apps, and work or school devices may have this controlled by an administrator — if there is no Turn on option, check model support / admin policy instead of forcing it.
steps.title: Turn on Google Play / Android apps, if supported and wanted

steps.detail: Linux is off by default. On a supported Chromebook: select the time at the bottom right > Settings > Advanced > Developers, next to 'Linux development environment' select Turn On, and follow the on-screen instructions using the default settings unless you need different ones. Setup can take 10 minutes or more and opens a Terminal window with a Debian environment. Linux lets you install command-line tools, code editors and IDEs.
steps.title: Optional: enable Linux (developers only)

honest_notes: Not all Chromebook models support Linux — Google directs users to check which devices have Linux, and notes that if you use your Chromebook at work or school you might not be able to use Linux; contact the administrator in that case.
Browse as Guest lets you use the Chromebook without an account, per Google, but it does not set an owner account and your signed-in bookmarks, extensions and apps will not appear that way.
disclaimers: Linux apps all run in the same sandbox as each other (separate from the rest of the Chromebook), and Google lists current limitations for Linux on Chromebook on its support page (for example cameras and hardware/GPU acceleration support limits at the time of the page consulted).

Google Play / Android app support also varies by model and by work/school management; the official page text retrieved for the Play turn-on flow in this session was thinner than the setup, update and Linux pages, so exact Settings labels are noted as version-dependent.

utility.name: Lenovo Vantage
sources: Lenovo Support — Lenovo Vantage - Using your PC just got easier (pcsupport.lenovo.com, HT505081)
Lenovo Support — Use Lenovo Vantage (download.lenovo.com user guide excerpt)
utility.what_it_does: Preinstalled / Microsoft Store app for Windows 10 and 11 Lenovo PCs. In the vendor's description it personalizes settings (power and battery life, audio/visual, camera/microphone, touchpad, Fn key and keyboard backlight), updates important system software and drivers including BIOS, runs device diagnostics / hardware scans, shows serial number, product number and BIOS level, checks warranty status, accesses the user guide, and lets the owner request support.

lenovo.driver_bios_channel: Primary: Lenovo Vantage System Update, which can download and install firmware and driver updates and can be configured for automatic updates. Alternative official routes: pcsupport.lenovo.com / support.lenovo.com — enter product name, serial number or machine type, open Drivers & Software for Manual Update or Automatic Update / Scan Now; BIOS can also be downloaded as an executable from the same Drivers & Software > BIOS/UEFI section. Lenovo System Update is listed as another official updater for Think / Lenovo systems. Lenovo Service Bridge can auto-detect system type and serial number on the support site.
setup_notes: Vantage replaces the older Lenovo Companion, Lenovo Settings and Lenovo Account Portal apps, per Lenovo's own Vantage page — a new owner should not look for those older apps.

Battery-specific Vantage features are officially documented, including battery health checks, battery details and a battery charge threshold setting, via Lenovo Support videos / Quick Tips linked from the Vantage page.

Lenovo also documents a Digital Download Recovery / USB recovery key route and UEFI Diagnostics separately from Vantage on pcsupport.lenovo.com — existence verified from Lenovo Support topic listings, full recovery steps not reviewed in this pass.

Standalone product registration steps for consumer PCs: not verified on official pages in this pass — only Lenovo ID creation, warranty lookup by serial, and registration for other Lenovo product families were found on official pages.
lenovo.warranty_registration: Warranty status is checked, not created, by serial number: on pcsupport.lenovo.com under Warranty & Services / Warranty Lookup, log in or enter the machine serial number to view status; the same status is visible in Lenovo Vantage. Lenovo ID is the vendor account — signing in gives purchase-history access used for warranty validation. A separate standalone PC product-registration flow with full steps was not detailed on the official PC support pages opened for this research — see setup_notes.

utility.name: Dell SupportAssist (for Home PCs)
sources: Dell Support — SupportAssist for Home PCs (dell.com/support contents article)
Dell — SupportAssist for Home PCs product/learn page (dell.com)
utility.what_it_does: Preinstalled on Dell PCs in Dell's description. It monitors PC health, performance and security in one dashboard, scans to proactively identify issues and start resolution, predicts failures including hard drive, battery and SSD, finds and installs available updates, removes unwanted files and tunes network settings, removes viruses/malware in Dell's description, and is the contact route to Dell technical support by phone, chat or messaging. Full feature set is tied in Dell's current pages to Dell Care Premium on top of the base warranty.

dell.driver_bios_channel: Primary: SupportAssist — it automatically scans for available updates and the owner acts via the notification or by opening SupportAssist and choosing Update Software. Alternative official route: Dell Support website — under Identify your product or search support, enter Service Tag, Express Service Code or model to reach that machine's drivers, manuals and warranty pages; Dell also offers a Detect This PC / View This PC option using SupportAssist to auto-detect the Service Tag. Dell Update / Dell Command Update are referenced by Dell as related update utilities in SupportAssist OS Recovery plugin material, but they were not the primary consumer route documented in this pass.
setup_notes: SupportAssist OS Recovery is a separate, factory-installed component on supported Dell systems and needs no extra service plan: if the PC repeatedly cannot boot to the OS it auto-starts a recovery environment to diagnose hardware, repair the computer, back up files, or reset to factory state — Dell SupportAssist for Home PCs page and SupportAssist OS Recovery User's Guide.
Dell Migrate / Dell Data Assistant is Dell's documented new-PC move-in route for moving files and personal settings from an old PC to a new Dell PC — linked from the SupportAssist for Home PCs page.
Minimum requirements Dell lists for current SupportAssist for Home PCs include Windows 10 version 1809 or later (64-bit) or Windows 11, .NET Desktop Runtime 6.0.x, and an active internet connection.
dell.warranty_registration: Every Dell PC ships with a base warranty in Dell's description. Warranty status and expiration are checked on Dell Support by entering the Service Tag or letting Dell's automated tool detect it. Dell's warranty KB groups check / renew / transfer / register together on its Support Services & Warranty page, and states the retail rule plainly: a computer bought through a retail seller must be registered with Dell to get personalized support — Dell Product Registration, distinct from a direct-from-Dell purchase.

utility.name: HP Support Assistant
sources: HP Support — HP Support Assistant (hp.com / HP Support Assistant help page)
utility.what_it_does: Included on new HP desktop and notebook PCs in HP's description, and installable on other PCs for HP printer/PC support access. HP lists: automated fixes and troubleshooters for common issues, with escalation to device-specific support resources if they do not resolve it; personalized support — manage connected HP devices after creating an HP ID or signing in, add another person's device for update/message notifications, and view available/subscribed HP services; automatic firmware and driver updates, configurable to install automatically or notify first; and help at any time via the HP Virtual Agent. Requires Windows 10 RS4 or higher for the current version in HP's note.

hp.driver_bios_channel: Primary: HP Support Assistant automatic updates for firmware and drivers, with owner-configurable automatic install vs. notify. Alternative official route: support.hp.com — Software & Drivers / Drivers & Software by product / serial, which HP staff also point to for the separate HP PC Hardware Diagnostics Windows download under Diagnostics. HP does not in the HPSA page opened for this pass present Windows Update as a substitute for HPSA for HP drivers.
setup_notes: HP's own HPSA page stresses sign-in: personalized device management and subscribed-service views need a new HP ID or existing credentials — a new owner who skips sign-in gets a reduced view.

HP registration prompt in Support Assistant during first setup: not verified on official pages in this pass — HP Community posts repeat 'register during first setup or soon afterwards' and link an HP Registration FAQ, but the FAQ body and an in-app prompt screenshot were not retrieved from support.hp.com here.

Separate diagnostics layer: HP PC Hardware Diagnostics (Windows and UEFI) exists as a distinct HP download/tool referenced from HP Support and HP Community staff answers — it is not described as part of HPSA itself on the HPSA page opened.

Coverage for HP is thinner than Lenovo/Dell/ASUS in this pass because several detailed HPSA guides surfaced only via HP Community or third-party mirrors, which were excluded per the official-sources-only rule.
hp.warranty_registration: Check route is well documented: support.hp.com/checkwarranty — use Identify now to let HP auto-identify the product and serial, or enter country/region plus serial number (single device, or Check multiple warranties for several) to see warranty status/details, with a warranty dispute/validation route if dates look wrong. In-app route referenced in HP material: HP Support Assistant My Dashboard > Warranty shows status, start and estimated end date. Registration itself: HP Community registration guidance says register the product during first setup or soon afterwards and points to a Register HP Product and Registration FAQ — the full text of that FAQ was not opened on an official page in this pass, so the exact first-setup registration prompt flow is marked thin below.

utility.name: MyASUS (plus Armoury Crate on ROG / TUF gaming lines)
sources: ASUS Support — MyASUS - Introduction (asus.com/support FAQ 1038301)
ASUS Support — MyASUS - System Diagnosis (asus.com/support FAQ 1045716)
ASUS Support — MyASUS - System Update (asus.com/support FAQ 1051729)
utility.what_it_does: Preinstalled on compatible ASUS computers and also in the Microsoft Store in ASUS's description. MyASUS provides: System Info and system-status monitoring; One-click diagnosis from the home page; Device Settings to fine-tune the laptop including Power & Performance (battery life/longevity), Audio & Visual, Connectivity, Input and Privacy & Security; System Diagnosis that identifies problems, reports sources and gives fixing suggestions and helps customer service identify problems; System Update for BIOS, drivers and firmware; Customer Support with FAQ/self-troubleshoot, ASUS Switch file backup, repair-status check and nearby repair-center search; Message Center; and User Center for account and product ownership.

asus.driver_bios_channel: Primary: MyASUS > System Update — ASUS describes it as updating the latest software including BIOS, drivers and firmware in one click, showing Critical / Recommended / Optional updates newer than the installed versions, with update history (not available in Windows S mode). Alternative official route: ASUS Support website — search the model to reach its support/download pages for drivers, BIOS and utilities, the route ASUS itself gives for manually downloading e.g. the Armoury Crate installer for a model. ASUS troubleshooting articles also route BIOS/Windows/driver updating through the MyASUS System Update article.
setup_notes: Armoury Crate is the gaming-line layer, separate from MyASUS: ASUS describes it as an integration app for ROG series and TUF series gaming laptops/desktops for system performance adjustments from its home page, system information, operating/performance modes and GPU modes, and Aura Sync lighting for the machine and supported external devices. ASUS's Armoury Crate FAQ states it is preinstalled for new ROG/TUF Gaming laptop/desktop owners and findable in the Start menu.

Battery diagnosis is a named MyASUS path in ASUS troubleshooting: MyASUS > System Diagnosis > Diagnosis Tool > Battery problems > Checkup, and ASUS advises contacting ASUS Product Support for replacement if battery health is bad.
Feature availability varies by model — ASUS repeatedly notes some devices show only partial MyASUS features, and System Diagnosis / System Update are not available in Windows S mode.
ASUS Switch (file backup when moving/repairing) is surfaced inside MyASUS Customer Support in ASUS's introduction — a setup-relevant move-in/backup note a new owner will encounter there.
asus.warranty_registration: Handled inside MyASUS User Center with an ASUS account: log in with ASUS ID (register one if needed), choose Instant product registration, type the product serial number and Send — the product then appears under My product. From the registered product, Product Footprint shows in one page the tech specs, repair status, warranty status and repair history, and offers Upgrade Warranty to buy an extension package; ASUS notes a newly bought extension refreshes the warranty end date within 3 to 5 days.

utility.name: Acer Care Center (ACC)
sources: Acer — Acer Care Center Application Security Issue with Update Mechanism (acer.com support alerts page)
Acer — Acer Care Center software page (acer.com, as listed in Acer Support search results)
utility.what_it_does: Acer's own current description is brief: the software on the device links the owner to Acer's support infrastructure for all support needs and provides services, checks and updates to keep the device updated and running smoothly. Acer's security-advisory page adds scope: Acer Care Center (and Acer Control Center) can be installed on any Acer consumer PC manufactured after 2014 running Windows 8.1 or a newer Windows OS, and its update mechanism verifies software/driver update authenticity. A fuller official feature breakdown (system info, checkup, tune-up, recovery) was not present on the official Acer pages retrieved in this pass — see setup_notes.

acer.driver_bios_channel: Primary official web route: Acer Support > Drivers and Manuals — identify the device first by entering serial number, SNID or model number to get that model's drivers, manuals and downloads (wording from Acer's own Drivers page listing). In-app route: Acer Care Center's check/update functions as described in Acer's broad 'checks and updates' wording and its Check for updates function in the advisory. Acer does not in the pages retrieved present a separate Acer BIOS updater app; BIOS files are part of the per-model Drivers and Manuals downloads.
setup_notes: Thin brand overall: Acer documents noticeably less first-setup guidance on its current official support/product pages than Lenovo, Dell or ASUS — that thinness is the honest result here, not a gap filled from blogs or community posts.
Acer Care Center registration inside the app: not verified on official pages in this pass — do not claim ACC registers the product or shows warranty dates without a further official-source check.

Detailed ACC features often listed elsewhere — My System info, PC Checkup for drives/battery/network, Tune-Up cleaners/startup manager, and Recovery Management backup/restore — were found in this pass only on non-official mirrors (e.g. FileHorse reproducing Acer copy) and Acer Community posts, so they are marked: not verified on official pages.

What is solid for a new owner from official Acer pages alone: install/keep ACC for support linkage and updates, and use acer.com Drivers and Manuals by serial/SNID/model for drivers, BIOS and manuals.
acer.warranty_registration: Thin on official pages retrieved: Acer Support exposes Warranty Information and warranty-status checking tied to identifying the product by serial/SNID on acer.com/support, and Acer manuals instruct owners to reach Service & Support via Care Center's Support link and the Drivers and Manuals serial/SNID/model search. A step-by-step official product-registration flow (Acer ID account + serial + purchase date) was not verified on official pages in this pass — third-party and Acer Community descriptions of it were excluded per the official-sources-only rule.

utility.name: Samsung Update / Samsung Device Care + Samsung Settings (Galaxy Book Experience apps)
sources: Samsung Support — How to use Device Care in Galaxy Book series (samsung.com/in/support/computing)
Samsung Support — How to use Battery and Performance feature in Galaxy Book series (samsung.com/in/support/computing)
Samsung Support — Galaxy Book Battery (samsung.com/us/support/galaxy-battery)
Samsung Download Center — Galaxy Book Guidance for Custom OS installation / driver package guide (downloadcenter.samsung.com)
utility.what_it_does: Samsung Update is Samsung's driver/software maintenance app for Galaxy Books: Samsung's own driver-package guidance describes Samsung Update (in the Optional folder of the driver package) as the tool to keep Samsung software up to date, and drivers can be installed/updated via Samsung Update or Windows Update. Current Samsung support centres on Samsung Device Care: per Samsung, it provides backup/restore, storage cleanup (temp/duplicate files), memory optimisation, factory reset, Maintenance Mode for repairs, online support (S Service), and an Updates section that keeps software, drivers, BIOS and apps up to date, with a Settings option for manual/auto driver updates. Samsung Settings is the hardware-settings companion: its Battery and performance section controls Battery protection (charge limit — 85% on the US Galaxy Book battery page, 90% in the India Battery and Performance article; model/region dependent), USB charging while off/hibernating, and Performance mode.

samsung.driver_bios_channel: Samsung Update app, or Samsung Device Care > Updates (keeps drivers, BIOS and apps current; manual/auto configurable in its Settings); also Windows Update. Model-specific driver packages/downloads are via Samsung support/download center for the exact model.
setup_notes: Sign in with both a Samsung Account and a Microsoft Account — Samsung Device Care lists this as a prerequisite note, and some features vary by country/region, model and Windows version.

Turn on Battery protection in Samsung Settings > Battery and performance if the laptop will live on AC power; Samsung says it limits maximum charge to prolong battery lifespan (85% US page / 90% India article — check the value shown for your model).
Protect battery applies to Galaxy Book3 and later models per Samsung's US battery page.
Samsung Members as the Galaxy Book warranty-registration channel: not verified on official pages in this research.
A Galaxy Book Experience as a single named suite page: not verified on official pages in this research — Samsung documents the individual apps (Samsung Settings, Device Care, Samsung Update) instead.
samsung.warranty_registration: Samsung support pages direct owners to register the product to see what is covered — Samsung's regional support home (samsung.com/my/support, as an example of Samsung's own support layout) lists Warranty: 'Register your product and find out what's covered.' Registration is tied to a Samsung account, and Samsung Device Care notes both a Samsung Account and a Microsoft Account should be signed in. A single canonical Galaxy Book-specific registration URL/flow was not verified on official pages in this research — see setup_notes.

utility.name: MSI Center
sources: MSI Support — MSI Center (NB SW_MSI_Center technical details, msi.com/support/technical_details)
MSI — MSI Center landing page (uk.msi.com/Landing/MSI-Center)
MSI Blog — MSI RTX 50 Laptop GPU Driver Update (msi.com/blog)
utility.what_it_does: MSI's exclusive app for its Gaming series laptops, per MSI's own technical-details page. Live Update scans and downloads/installs driver updates; User Scenario offers Extreme Performance, Balanced, Silent, Super Battery and a custom User mode (performance level and fan speed, GPU overclock on some models); Gaming Mode auto-tunes a selected game; System Diagnosis includes Battery Master (battery health view, charging modes including Balanced and Best for Battery charge limits, and battery calibration, which MSI recommends every 3 months) and System Checker (disk cleanup, memory freeing, SSD model/capacity/temperature/health); Hardware Monitoring shows real-time CPU/GPU usage; Mystic Light controls LED effects; General Settings covers items such as Windows-key and graphics-mode (MSHybrid vs discrete) toggles, varying by model.

msi.driver_bios_channel: Primary: MSI Center > Support > Live Update — Scan, select the driver, Download; some drivers auto-install (reboot after), others open an unzipped folder for manual install per MSI's driver-update instructions on its support page. MSI's blog directs laptop owners to the same Live Update route for GPU drivers after Windows setup. Manual alternative: download drivers/BIOS for the exact model from the model's product support/download page on msi.com. BIOS via Live Update is documented for some lines (e.g. MSI Center M notes BIOS update through Live Update); model support pages remain the fallback — BIOS availability by model was not uniformly verified on official pages.
setup_notes: Run Live Update once after Windows setup — MSI notes some MSI Center functions (e.g. Microsoft APP downloads) require a first Live Update system analysis.

MSI's own laptop GPU-driver article recommends updating the GPU driver before first use, either from the on-screen prompt after Windows setup/restart or manually via MSI Center > Support > Live Update, staying online and not powering off during the update.
Battery Master charge-limit modes differ by selection (e.g. Balanced stops at 80%, Best for Battery at 60% per MSI's page) — a new-owner setting worth choosing deliberately.
Feature sets are modular/customisable in current MSI Center per MSI's landing page — only install the feature sets needed.
msi.warranty_registration: Register the product in the MSI Member Center (account.msi.com): become an MSI Member, log in, and register the product with its details — MSI's official Extended Warranty Service Manual (download-2.msi.com) describes exactly this flow, with extended-warranty activation done afterwards in Member Center via Product Activation using the service code/password from the purchased Extended Warranty Digital Membership Card.

LG USA Support — LG Gram: How to Factory Reset Using the LG Recovery Center App (lg.com/us/support/help-library)
LG UK Support — Manual and Software / LG Update (lg.com/uk/support)
utility.what_it_does: LG's model-matched update app. Per LG's installation guide, an integrated LG Update apps launcher installs the LG Update app suitable for the PC, and with the installed app 'the latest drivers and programs can be used optimally.' The variant that runs depends on release date: LG Update / LG Update & Recovery for products released after April 2022; LG Update Center and LG DNA Center Plus for products released before April 2022. LG product-support pages also surface related help items such as LG Recovery Center for factory reset (separate from the update app).

lg.driver_bios_channel: Run the LG Update Program to launch the compatible LG Update app and install/update drivers and LG programs from its Required Updates / Update list (as also described in LG gram manual material). The Update app itself is installed via the LG Update Installer from the Microsoft Store (or LG's download link). Fallback/manual route: LG's website download library / model product-support page (Software & Drivers) for the exact model and OS. LG cautions that installing a different OS than the pre-installed one may prevent the Update Program from installing drivers/software, and recommends the pre-installed OS.
setup_notes: First step for a new gram owner per LG: install/run the LG Update Installer (Microsoft Store) — it auto-updates itself and installs the LG Update app compatible with that system, then offers 'LG Update & Recovery Run'.
Variant names are date-dependent (see utility) — do not look for 'LG Update Center' by name on a post-April-2022 machine.

LG gram software notes beyond the Update family (e.g. LG Control Center / LG Smart Assistant functions referenced in gram manuals for touchpad and settings): partially documented in LG manual/help material; a single official gram software overview page was not verified on official pages in this research.
Warranty registration path: not verified on official pages (see warranty_registration).
lg.warranty_registration: not verified on official pages — LG's laptop help-library and product-support pages reviewed for this research document driver/software downloads, repair requests and LG Premium Care, but no specific laptop warranty-registration path (account, URL or steps) was verified on official LG pages in this research.

utility.name: Surface app (with Windows Update as the driver/firmware channel) + Surface Diagnostic Toolkit
sources: Microsoft Support — Fix common problems using the Surface app and Surface Diagnostic Toolkit (support.microsoft.com)
Microsoft Support — Using the Surface Diagnostic Toolkit (support.microsoft.com)
Microsoft Support — Download drivers and firmware for Surface (support.microsoft.com)
Microsoft Support — Check your Microsoft warranty and create service orders (support.microsoft.com)
utility.what_it_does: The Surface app is the owner hub: per Microsoft Support, in the Surface app you can check driver/firmware health and update status under Help & support (with a Check for updates button that opens Windows Update), get help / surface detected issues, and view warranty under Warranty & services. The separate Surface Diagnostic Toolkit runs guided checks/repairs — Microsoft lists tests for Windows update and system repair, power supply and battery, touchscreen/display brightness, speakers/microphone, network connectivity, and memory/storage; it is downloaded from the Microsoft Store if not pre-installed.

microsoft.driver_bios_channel: Windows Update is the primary channel: Settings > Windows Update > Check for updates (attach Surface dock/Type Cover/accessories so they receive updates too), plus View optional updates for additional Surface-named driver updates. The Surface app's Help & support > Check for updates jumps to the same place. Manual/offline alternative per Microsoft: download the model-specific .msi driver+firmware package from Microsoft's Download drivers and firmware for Surface page / Download Center. Firmware updates cannot be uninstalled or reverted, per Microsoft's update-history notes.
setup_notes: Install/open the Surface app (Microsoft Store if missing) and use Help & support to confirm update status before troubleshooting anything else — Microsoft's recommended first check.
Run the Surface Diagnostic Toolkit for guided hardware/software checks if something is not working; Microsoft notes diagnosis/repair averages about 15 minutes but can take longer.
Keep the device plugged in and connected to the internet, with accessories attached, when checking Windows Update so firmware for the device and accessories installs together.
Manual .msi packages are positioned by Microsoft for troubleshooting, offline devices, multi-device deployment and imaging — not the normal new-owner route.
microsoft.warranty_registration: Via the Microsoft account. Microsoft Support states you may need to register your Surface to your account before checking warranty or getting service: at account.microsoft.com/devices, if the device is not listed, select Register device and add it (serial number); then select the device > Info & support to see Device coverage type and remaining time. Warranty/coverage dates are also visible in the Surface app under Warranty & services. If the warranty date does not match the purchase date, Microsoft provides an Update your Surface warranty with proof-of-purchase flow. The task brief's claim that a Surface registers automatically simply by signing in was not stated in those terms on the Microsoft pages reviewed — Microsoft describes registration as an account action at account.microsoft.com/devices when the device is not already listed.

utility.name: None — no separate vendor utility; System Settings > General > Software Update handles updates
sources: Apple Support — Update macOS on Mac (support.apple.com)
Apple Support — Software Update settings on Mac (support.apple.com guide)
Apple Support — About background updates in macOS (support.apple.com)
Apple Support — System Information User Guide for Mac (support.apple.com)
utility.what_it_does: There is no Apple equivalent of MSI Center/Synapse for Mac laptops. Built-in System Settings does the job: Software Update settings (Apple menu > System Settings > General > Software Update) find, download and install Apple software updates/upgrades compatible with that Mac model, with Automatic Updates options to download new updates when available, install macOS updates automatically, and install Security Responses / system files (and background security/system-data updates, which Apple says install automatically by default). System Information (About) is Apple's built-in hardware/software report tool and points to warranty/repair information via About settings.

apple.driver_bios_channel: Software Update only. Apple delivers macOS, firmware, drivers and security updates together through System Settings > General > Software Update (or Spotlight search for 'Software Update'); Apple states Software Update shows only software compatible with your Mac model and is the fastest/easiest route, using less storage than other methods. There is no separate Apple driver/BIOS download channel for Mac laptops. Back up the Mac before installing, and allow installation to complete without sleeping/closing the lid (multiple restarts/progress bars are normal, per Apple).
setup_notes: New-owner step per Apple: open Software Update, let it check automatically, install what is offered, and turn on the Automatic Updates options you want (download when available, install macOS updates, install security/system files).
Mac laptops must have the power adapter plugged in to automatically download updates, per Apple's Keep your Mac up to date guide (older macOS wording).
There are no third-party-style driver packs to hunt down — if Software Update says the Mac is up to date, Apple offers no additional model driver downloads.

checkcoverage.apple.com / mysupport.apple.com coverage-check flow: not verified on official pages in this research (only the on-device About / AppleCare & Warranty route was verified on support.apple.com).
apple.warranty_registration: No product-registration step is required to have Apple Limited Warranty coverage documented in this research. Coverage can be reviewed on the Mac itself — Apple Support's System Information guide directs users to About settings for warranty and repair-service information, and current macOS exposes AppleCare & Warranty under System Settings > General. The checkcoverage.apple.com serial-number checker and My Support (Apple Account) device list referenced in the task brief were not verified on official Apple pages returned in this research — see setup_notes.

utility.name: None — no preinstalled vendor utility; Framework Driver Bundle (downloaded installer) + Framework guides
sources: Framework Guides — Windows 11 Installation on the Framework Laptop 13 (guides.frame.work)
Framework Guides — Upgrading to Windows 11 from Windows 10 on the Framework Laptop (guides.frame.work)
Framework Community — Framework Laptop 16 AMD Ryzen 7040 Driver Bundle release posts (community.frame.work)
utility.what_it_does: Framework ships no MSI Center-style preinstalled control app. The setup layer is the downloadable Framework Laptop Driver Bundle: per Framework's own Windows 11 installation guide, after Windows installation you download the bundle for your Mainboard/generation and run it, and it automatically installs all drivers required to use the laptop (several minutes, then press a key to reboot). DIY assembly, repair and upgrade steps live as step-by-step guides at guides.frame.work (e.g. the Windows 11 Installation guide for the Framework Laptop 13 DIY Edition, which assumes memory, storage and Wi-Fi are installed first).

framework.driver_bios_channel: Drivers: download and run the generation-specific Driver Bundle from frame.work (linked from the guides); if the machine has no network yet, download it on another system and copy it via USB flash drive. The guide also notes an OOBE Wi-Fi driver package placed on the Windows install USB so networking works during setup. After the bundle, run Windows Update — Framework's guides state future driver and firmware updates can also come through Windows Update. BIOS: separate downloadable BIOS updaters announced on community.frame.work / downloads.frame.work — Windows .exe installer (run, agree to reboot, wait for the firmware progress bar), Linux via LVFS/fwupdmgr, or UEFI Shell update from a FAT32 USB (suspend BitLocker first if using the EFI updater with Windows); charger must be attached.
setup_notes: DIY Edition order of operations per Framework's guide: install memory, storage and Wi-Fi first, install Windows, then install the Driver Bundle to get the laptop fully functional — a fresh Windows install may lack drivers for the new hardware, and the touchpad runs in a limited compatibility mode until the bundle is installed.
Put the OOBE Wi-Fi driver package on the install USB in advance so the 'Let's connect you to a network' setup screen can load a driver and show networks.
BIOS/driver release notifications: Framework's BIOS release posts offer an opt-in email subscription for new BIOS/driver releases for your laptop.

Framework's explicit 'no-bloatware' stance as a documented setup claim: not verified on official pages in this research — what is verified is the absence of a preinstalled vendor utility and the manual Driver Bundle step in Framework's own guide.
framework.warranty_registration: Via your Framework account/order and Framework Support — the Windows guide directs owners who bought Windows from Framework to log into their Framework account (Digital Purchases) for their key, and closes by directing questions to Framework Support via frame.work. No separate warranty-registration form or serial-registration flow was verified on official Framework pages in this research — support is order/account-based as documented.

Find your exact model first (Razer Support: 'How to identify a Razer Blade model' and serial/product-number finders) — BIOS updaters and driver downloads are model-specific (RZ09-xxxx).
BIOS access documented by Razer Support: tap F1 or Del at the Razer logo on startup, or via Windows Advanced startup > UEFI Firmware Settings.
Warranty registration via Razer ID: not verified on official pages (see warranty_registration).
